triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. De-wiki: Jun to early winter, mainly Jul-Oct; fungiversum Aug-Nov. Occurs up to the forest limit.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Pinus is only secondary (en-wiki lists it; de-wiki names Betula and Picea as the main partners). Elevation 300-1800 not verifiable, sources only say up to forest limit.

triggers: Fruiting follows heavy rainfall (fungiversum). Fertilised lawns and nutrient-rich disturbed soil. Fruits Apr-Nov (de-wiki), Mar-Dec (fungiversum).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Elevation 100-1500 not verified: fungiversum only says present up to subalpine zone. Months in catalogue fine (sources wider: Apr-Nov, Mar-Dec).

triggers: Weather dependent (de-wiki). Avoids very dry and waterlogged soil. No numeric thresholds stated. Fruits from May, into Oct or later (de-wiki), May-Nov (tintling).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue season starts Jun; three sources give May start. Catalogue Abies/Fagus ok but spruce is the main partner. Some authors treat N. luridiformis as a synonym; elevation 400-1600 not verifiable.

triggers: Fresh to moist soil, rare on persistently dry sites (de-wiki). No numeric triggers. De-wiki: Jun to early Nov, occasionally mid-Apr; fungiversum Jul-Oct.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Carpinus not named by the sources opened (catalogue lists it); Abies/Picea are secondary. Soil is weakly acid to weakly alkaline, so not acid-bound. Elevation 200-1400 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. De-wiki: Aug-Nov; en-wiki: Jul-Dec in Europe. Attached by rhizomorphs; only puffball on wood in Central Europe.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue starts Jul; de-wiki Aug-Nov, en-wiki Jul-Dec. No host genera, habitat type or elevation stated in sources, so left empty.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Often forms fairy rings. Sep-Nov, sometimes into early winter (pilzkurse); en-wiki Aug-Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue starts Aug (en-wiki agrees); pilzkurse gives Sep-Nov with early-winter tail. Elevation 200-1400 not verifiable.

triggers: Spring; low-temperature germination, soil temperature linked to spore germination (en-wiki). Also on recently burnt or dug soil. Numbers not stated. Romanian source: from April, damp edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat W understates orchards, gardens, scrub. Sources describe saprotroph with tree association, not mycorrhiza; Dutch elm disease sites noted. Season Apr-Jun in de-wiki/fungiversum, ro source Apr-May. Absent from high mountains (de-wiki); 100-1000 unverified.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Jun-Oct (fungiversum).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Corylus is only an occasional partner (fungiversum: almost exclusively Carpinus). Only one source with ecology detail; elevation, pH, abundance not stated.

triggers: Clumps arise after rainfall (en-wiki); can fruit repeatedly in a year. No numeric thresholds.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season May-Nov matches (tintling). Tintling says occurs in all biotopes in and outside forests. Elevation 100-1200 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. En-wiki: fruits throughout the mushroom season; no months given by other source.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue elevation up to 2000 contradicted: pilze-ammersee says mainly lowlands, replaced by B. nigrescens in the Alps. Catalogue implies commonness; pilze-ammersee says fairly rare and overlooked. Months unverified so left null.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Warm-loving, southern distribution in Europe. Jun-Sep (de-wiki); summer to early autumn (en-wiki).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent with catalogue. En-wiki: rare in most localities. Elevation 100-800 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Fungiversum: Jul-Oct; en-wiki summer to autumn. Prefers sandy substrate.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says acid sandy soils only; de-wiki and fungiversum: acid and basic soils, sandy preferred. Castanea not stated by sources (catalogue lists it); Fagus named by de-wiki and fungiversum. Season runs to Oct. Red-listed in several countries.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Fungiversum: Jun-Nov; en-wiki: late summer. Often with heather on sandy soil.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent. Catalogue elevation 300-1500 and abundance not verifiable; sources give no elevation.

triggers: Main fruiting mid-Sep to Nov before first frost, from Aug (ciupercar.ro). Very moist soils. De-wiki: mid-Aug to late Nov, esp. Sep-Oct. No numeric thresholds.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jul-Oct; sources give Aug-Nov (peak Sep-Oct), none starts in Jul. Soil: sources say calcareous, moist, heavy; catalogue silent. Elevation: de-wiki says mid-elevation mountain zones, no numbers.

triggers: Needs enough rain beforehand and strong warmth (de-wiki, fungiversum). En-wiki: lab mycelial growth optimum 24-28 C, not a fruiting threshold. Warm, fairly dry sites (ciupercar.ro).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Soil: de-wiki and ciupercar.ro say acid, sandy, base-poor; catalogue silent. Season sources: Jun-Oct (ro), Jul-Nov, Jun-Sep (ro); main Jul-Oct. Romanian source: found in mountain and lowland, so elevation 100-700 not confirmed. Rare in RO and declining.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Warm-loving regions; fungiversum: Jul-Oct.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jun start; only fungiversum gives months (Jul-Oct). Both sources: calcareous, rare. Elevation 100-700 not verifiable.

triggers: Fruits Jun-Oct depending on local moisture and temperature (ciupercar.ro). Fairy rings on old orchard meadows (de-wiki).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Nettle beds not mentioned by sources; they list meadows, pastures, orchards, gardens, light woods incl. loose pine on dry sites. Elevation 100-1200 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Jul-Oct (de-wiki).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent. Soil mainly acid to moderately acid, also on calcareous (de-wiki). Synonym R. mairei. Elevation 300-1300 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Jul-Nov (fungiversum), Jun-Nov (de-wiki). Fresh to moist, mossy spruce stumps.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says conifer and broadleaf; sources: Picea mainly, Fagus and Pinus secondary. Acid, nutrient-poor soil. Elevation 300-1500 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Fungiversum Jul-Oct; de-wiki Aug-Dec.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue lists only Fagus and Quercus; sources also give Pinus, Picea, Abies. De-wiki: decline in western Central Europe since the 1970s. Elevation 300-1200 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Summer to late autumn (123pilzsuche); June to fall (mushroomexpert, North America).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says parasite on oak roots; sources: parasitic or secondary decomposer, base of living or dead trees, buried wood. Catalogue season Aug-Oct unverified, sources only say summer-autumn. Extremely rare in Germany.

triggers: Spring species on buried cones of previous year; needs moist conditions (fungiversum). Tintling Apr-May; fungiversum Oct-May.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Feb-May: tintling gives Apr-May, fungiversum Oct-May; Feb-Mar not confirmed. Elevation 500-1600 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Aug-Nov (both sources). Moss-rich soils.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources say more common at mid to high altitude but give no numbers; catalogue 800-1700 not verifiable. De-wiki also mentions calcareous soils.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Aug-Oct (fungiversum); Jul-Oct (de-wiki); summer to late autumn (pilzwelten).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent. De-wiki: among the most frequent Cortinarius in DE, AT, CH; also on sandy or moorland soils. Elevation 400-1700 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Spring: Apr-Jun (natur-in-nrw), May-Jun (fungiversum).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat W is misleading: sources describe hedges, scrub, path edges, parks, gardens, meadows. Malus not named; Prunus (plum, blackthorn), Crataegus, Pyrus, Sorbus named. Nowhere frequent (natur-in-nrw).

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. De-wiki Apr-May; fungiversum Apr-Jun.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says floodplain and damp broadleaf only; sources add moist humus-rich meadows, gardens, parks, scrub, stream banks, with no tree association stated. Elevation 100-900 not verifiable. Rare and protected in Germany.

triggers: Ripens from mid-Sep, edible from Oct, hunted in winter (de-wiki); Aug-Feb (trueffelsuche). Warm sites. No numeric triggers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jan-Mar and Nov-Dec; sources say Aug/Sep to Feb, none supports Mar. Fagus and Tilia named by de-wiki (catalogue has Quercus, Corylus). Abundance disagreement: de-wiki very rare in Germany, trueffelsuche one of four frequent species. Elevation not stated.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Jul-Oct (all three sources).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says montane Picea only, 800-1700 m: de-wiki says lowlands to uplands, derkleinegarten says rarer in mountainous regions. Soil disagreement: de-wiki acid to neutral, pilzmuseum calcareous. Pine also named (pilzmuseum).

triggers: Fruits until first frosts of early winter, especially abundant after hot summers (natur-in-nrw). Sep to late Nov (tintling). No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat floodplain not confirmed: sources list poplar avenues, parks, roadsides, plantings, stands on sandy-loamy grassy ground. Salix occasional. Elevation 100-600 not stated.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Pilzmuseum Jul-Nov; en-wiki from June.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue lists Abies and calcareous soil: sources name Fagus and Picea (en-wiki) or just broadleaf trees (pilzmuseum), soils of all kinds with preference for some base content. Elevation 400-1300 not verifiable.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. June-Nov (tintling); early summer to autumn (123pilzsuche).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jul-Oct; sources Jun-Nov. Elevation 100-800 not stated. Widely distributed but not particularly common.

triggers: No rain amount, lag or temperature threshold stated in sources consulted. Aug-Oct (tintling), Aug-Nov (pilz-sammler).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue lists Pinus: sources say various broadleaf and conifer trees, specifically Quercus, Betula, Fagus. Soil sandy, acid, nutrient-poor (tintling). Elevation 200-1200 not stated.

triggers: Found nearly all year; frost-resistant, can be dug out under snow in winter (de.wikipedia). Most common in autumn (en.wikipedia); first-nature also says mainly winter/spring. No rain or temperature numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Elevation 100-1000 m unverified (no source gives altitude). Sources call it a weak parasite on living wood as well as saprotroph. Conifers (Picea) only very rarely. Sources disagree on peak (autumn vs winter/spring).

triggers: Native Central European strains need temps below 11 C to fruit and tolerate frost down to -2.8 C (Bresinsky, via de.wikipedia). Historically a winter mushroom; also summer to early winter in first-nature.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Populus and Salix not named in fetched sources (beech, oaks, 'other hardwoods'); rarely conifers. Catalogue months include Jan-Apr; sources describe autumn-early winter (winter strain), so Jan-Mar possible but not quantified. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers in sources. Prefers moderately dry, base- and nutrient-poor soils; on limestone only superficially acidified soil (de.wikipedia). Often in young plantations and sparse moss/grass spots.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources give Jun-Nov (de) / Jun-Oct to Nov (first-nature), catalogue Jun-Oct. Preferred partner in Central Europe is Picea, then Fagus; Pinus missing from catalogue. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany, no RO source.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers. Avoids waterlogged, rapidly drying, alkaline and nutrient-rich soils; sandy to slightly loamy, acid to neutral soils (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue starts in June; de.wikipedia gives Jul-Oct for Central Europe (Jun mentioned for the genus in general). 'Conifers' = Picea in sources; Carpinus added. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers. In Central Europe mainly in higher parts of the low mountain ranges, very rare at low elevation (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Soil: de.wikipedia says acid soils preferred; first-nature and en.wikipedia say alkaline/neutral/chalky - sources disagree. Season Jul-Dec in sources vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Abies not named as partner; Quercus added. Higher-elevation tendency supported, numbers not.

triggers: Prefers warm sites for fruiting (de.wikipedia). Emerges from wounds and cavities of living or dead standing hardwoods, sometimes several metres up. No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue Jun-Sep; sources Jun-Oct (de) and Jul-Nov (first-nature). Substrate sources differ: living/dead standing trees (de, en) vs dead trunks (first-nature). Rare in Germany; elevation unverified.

triggers: No rain/temperature numbers stated. Mainly in conifer forests, less often broadleaf.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue omits Picea, which de.wikipedia names first (Fichten, Birken); Pinus/Betula supported by first-nature. Association with Amanita muscaria not stated in sources. Catalogue starts Jun; source says Jul-Oct. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Typically nutrient-rich soils in forests and parks, few special requirements (de.wikipedia); also reported in grasslands and hardwood/conifer woods (en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Neither source states a mycorrhizal host; trophic mode 'm' and host list are not confirmed. Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Jun-Oct. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany.

triggers: No numbers. Moist, loamy, calcareous soils in mixed deciduous forest (de.wikipedia); first-nature notes woodland edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources Aug-Nov (de) vs catalogue Sep-Nov. Oak also named as partner. en.wikipedia (mostly North American) says mostly coniferous woods, which disagrees with de/first-nature (beech). Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Appears mostly in autumn and late autumn (de.wikipedia); clusters at base of living or dead trunks.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue months. Sources say saprobic or weakly parasitic on living or dead wood, also conifers (Picea) occasionally; apple (Malus) at trunk base named by de.wikipedia. Elevation unverified. Abundance from Germany ('very common').

triggers: Thermophilic: warm, south-facing limestone sites (tintling). Main season July-August (pilzbuch-pilzwelten); late Jul to mid Sep, rarely early Oct (tintling). No rain numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue months roughly (sources Jun-Aug to early Oct). Beech is the main partner in German sources; oak per en.wikipedia (southern Europe). Rare in most Central European limestone areas. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Mostly beech, beech-fir, oak-hornbeam and spruce-fir forests; avoids pure spruce stands (de.wikipedia). Less common in lowlands, more in low mountain ranges (en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Picea (secondary) and Quercus named by sources; Abies only 'rarely'. Months consistent (Jul-Oct to Jul-Nov). Low-mountain tendency supported, numeric 400-1200 m not.

triggers: No numbers. Strictly bound to larch; mainly on lime-rich soils (de.wikipedia); calcareous or sandy soils (first-nature). Alpine-subalpine and montane areas.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent with catalogue (Larix, Jul-Oct). Adds lime-rich soil preference. Described as uncommon to rare in en.wikipedia, not very dense in de. Elevation 500-1600 m unverified.

triggers: Rainy weather can bring fruitbodies as early as July (de.wikipedia). Acid, base- and nutrient-poor, moderately to clearly moist soils, among mosses; often fruits in large numbers. No rain numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Months consistent (Aug-Nov, July after rain). Deciduous partners (beech) occasional. en.wikipedia describes North American hosts and Nov-Jan season, not applicable to Europe. Elevation 600-1700 m unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Also on grassy forest edges and unkept lawns (de/en.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names specific host genera (only 'both conifer and broadleaf forests'), so hosts left empty. Months match (Jun-Oct de; Jul-Oct first-nature). Elevation unverified. Abundance 'common, widely distributed' (de, en), 'infrequent' in Britain.

triggers: No numbers. Saprotroph in woods, especially in needle litter under spruce (de.wikipedia); in all kinds of woodland (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (Jul-Nov) vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Litter is mostly conifer (spruce) per de.wikipedia; first-nature says all woodland. Elevation unverified. Spelled silvicola in de/en wikipedia.

triggers: No numbers. Acidified, sandy, well-drained soils, forest tracks, shaded banks and drainage-ditch sides (de.wikipedia, first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names host genera (Quercus, Betula, Pinus unconfirmed); de.wikipedia stresses dry sandy conifer and mixed forests. Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Prefers acid sandy, loamy or silicate soils but tolerates limestone (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources name many more partners (Abies, Betula, Carpinus, Quercus) than catalogue (Fagus, Picea). Season Jun-Oct (de), Jul-Nov (first-nature); Jul-Oct kept. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Acid, fresh soils; rare or absent in calcareous areas; warm oak and oak-hornbeam forests, also beech forests (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent with catalogue (Quercus, Jul-Oct). Castanea only in southern Europe. Never fruits in large numbers in Germany (scattered to rare), common in UK. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue says broadleaf and conifer. de.wikipedia: deciduous partners; conifer records may be related species; first-nature still says broadleaf and conifer. Disagreement. Months Aug-Nov vs Jun-Oct UK; catalogue kept. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Fruits April to late October and in mild winter spells (en.wikipedia); all year, most plentiful in summer-autumn (first-nature). Often when few other fungi are out.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue includes Nov; sources say Apr-Oct plus mild winters. Birch/beech/alder named; rarely conifers. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Lying trunks, stumps and dead roots of spruce; benefits from forestry planting of spruce and pine (de.wikipedia).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent (Jul-Nov, conifer wood). Very rarely on broadleaf wood. Elevation 500-1600 m unverified; very common in German planted spruce stands at all levels.

triggers: No numbers. Lean meadows and pastures in hill country, also forest clearings (de.wikipedia); closely mown unfertilised grassland, upland acid pastures (first-nature). Intolerant of heavy fertiliser.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Sep-Nov (de) vs Aug-Dec (first-nature); catalogue Aug-Nov. Montane tendency ('im Bergland') but no altitude numbers; catalogue 300-2000 m unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Autumn species; earliest at higher altitudes (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Picea not confirmed (sources say only 'occasionally conifers'). Soil: en.wikipedia acidic vs first-nature alkaline/chalk - disagree. Not common anywhere in Europe. Season Jul-Nov (first-nature) broader than catalogue. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Groups and fairy rings in broadleaf woodland and woodland edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No source names Fagus or a mycorrhizal host; trophic mode unconfirmed. Season Jul-Oct (pilzfinder, var. nidorosum) / summer to late autumn (first-nature) vs catalogue Aug-Oct. Abundance 'very common' only from UK source. Elevation unverified.

triggers: Early spring after snowmelt, around leaf-out, before true morels (en.wikipedia). Does not fruit every year; warm sites, often in floodplains (de.wikipedia). Cited 3-30 C range is mycelial growth, not fruiting.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Fraxinus not named in sources (poplar, willow, aspen near riverbanks). Catalogue includes March; de.wikipedia gives Apr-May. Locally common on calcareous floodplain soils, otherwise rare. Elevation unverified.

triggers: July-August rain essential for fruiting (trufamania); tolerates summer rain up to 180% of normal, drought reduces mycelium; fruitbodies need at least 0.4 C during winter formation (en.wikipedia). Soil pH ~7.7.
conflicts_with_catalogue: No fetched source records it in Romania (Italy, Istria, Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia etc.); Romanian occurrence unconfirmed. Season Sep-early Jan (de) / late Sep-late Nov. Oak is most frequent host; poplar secondary. Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Warm beech forests on base-rich, nutrient-poor soils (lime, marl); some forms fruit at snowbank edges in spring in North America (en.wikipedia, not Europe).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Consistent (Fagus, Quercus, Jul-Oct; de Aug-Oct, first-nature Jul-Nov). Pine only in warmer regions. Rare and declining in Germany (RL 2). Elevation unverified.

triggers: No numbers. Warm summer months, occasionally to October (de.wikipedia). Basic, dry to fresh soils; sedge-beech and oak-hornbeam forests.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Carpinus not named as partner (only as forest type); beech and oak lead. Season Jul-Oct vs catalogue Jun-Sep. Lower altitudes supported (en.wikipedia), 100-800 m not numerically confirmed. Red List 3 in Germany, endangered in Czechia.

triggers: No numbers. Main season end of August to end of October (de.wikipedia). Grows on acid, neutral and alkaline soils; abundant even on thin soil and steep run-off slopes (first-nature).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Jul-Nov vs catalogue Aug-Nov. Lowland, hill and lower montane, rarely higher (de.wikipedia), consistent with 100-900 m but no numbers.

triggers: No rain/frost numbers. Lean, nutrient-poor grazed grassland; avoids forest and calcareous areas (de.wikipedia). Mild sites occasionally to January. Observed in quantity at 1400-1700 m (Tirol) and 820-1300 m (Black Forest).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season Aug-Oct (to Jan locally) vs catalogue Aug-Nov. Lowland to alpine in sources; 400-2000 m not stated as a range. en.wikipedia says rich acidic soil; de says nutrient-poor.

triggers: No numbers. Examined collections from September and October (czechmycology). Moist places along creeks, paths and roadsides, with Urtica or Rubus; well-decayed wood, twigs, acorns, cones.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: mostly broadleaved or mixed forest, less often conifer (catalogue stresses mixed and conifer). Not specifically buried wood. Season rests on Sep-Oct records only. 'Common in Central Europe' (en.wikipedia) vs 'very poorly known' (czechmycology). Probably submontane-montane.

triggers: No numeric triggers in sources; fruits Jun-Oct, under favourable weather to Dec (de.wikipedia). Weather only said to influence appearance.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Wikipedia names spruce and beech as main partners; catalogue 'broadleaf and conifer' is correct but generic. No elevation data found (catalogue 200-1600 unverified). Abundance is from Germany/Europe-wide statements.

triggers: No triggers stated. Sources say Aug-Oct (some Nov) late-season; tintling.com and pilzmuseum.at give May-Oct with autumn the main period.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Months broadly agree (catalogue Aug-Nov). Sources describe beech (also oak-hornbeam) litter on base-rich soil, a calcicole indicator. Rare in high southern Germany; no elevation range found (catalogue 200-1000 unverified). en.wikipedia lists Romania in range.

triggers: No triggers stated. Fruits on wood of any decay stage; late Apr/May to Nov, practically year-round in Germany (tintling.com).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season matches catalogue. Sources name broadleaf wood (maple, birch, beech, oak) mainly, rarely conifers, though tintling.com says beech and spruce. No elevation data (catalogue 100-1500 unverified). Abundance from Germany/Central Europe.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources give May-Nov; catalogue starts in June. No elevation data (catalogue 200-1800 unverified). Described as one of the most common fungi in Europe.

triggers: No triggers stated. Jul-Oct per de.wikipedia (rarely in spring); Jun-Oct per pilzlexikon.eu.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: broadleaf trees, esp. beech (also oak-hornbeam forest, parks); pilzlexikon says both broadleaf and conifer partners but names no genera. Season Jun/Jul-Oct, catalogue Jul-Oct. Elevation not found.

triggers: No weather triggers stated. Weak parasite of old living oaks; bark injuries are entry points. Fruits Jul-Oct/Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts and months match. Sources: thermophilic oak-hornbeam forest, preferably calcareous, collinar to submontane; 'nirgends haeufig'/rare. Catalogue 100-800 m not numerically confirmed.

triggers: No numeric triggers. Late season; continues into December in frost-free periods (pilz-baden.ch). Forms fairy rings.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season matches. Sources: humus-rich beech forests, spruce plantations, oak-hornbeam, fresh to moderately moist soils; very common. No elevation data (catalogue 200-1500 unverified).

triggers: No triggers stated; grows on dung, old manure heaps and fertilised meadows.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Season May-Oct matches. en.wikipedia says year-round in warm climates (N. America). No elevation data (catalogue 200-1800 unverified).

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: de.wikipedia: Aug-Oct, mainly deciduous (base-rich beech) forest, rarely mixed; other sources say summer-autumn and conifer/mixed forest. Catalogue Jul-Oct and 'broadleaf and conifer' only partly supported. Elevation not found.

triggers: No numeric triggers; dung and manured pasture, esp. subalpine pastures (Almwiesen).
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: May-Nov (de.wikipedia) vs (Jun)Sep-Oct (pilzfreun.de); catalogue May-Oct. Mostly subalpine pastures, rare at intermediate elevation, 'nicht haeufig'; catalogue 100-2000 m not confirmed.

triggers: Fruits in warm spells in summer/early autumn (en.wikipedia); heat-loving, increasing with warming (de.wikipedia). No numbers.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue habitat G (grass/parks) not supported; sources say broadleaf forest. de.wikipedia: needs lime-rich soil; en.wikipedia: both calcareous and acidic soils (disagreement). Parks not mentioned. Catalogue 100-700 m unconfirmed.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Catalogue host Populus tremula: de.wikipedia ties aspen strictly to L. leucopodium, so aspen is likely a different taxon. en.wikipedia: poplar traditionally, plus oak and other broadleaves. pilzlexikon covers L. quercinum (oak), so it is only indirect support. Taxonomy unsettled.

triggers: No triggers stated. Late Aug-Oct, occasionally earlier or to Nov.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Host and season match. de.wikipedia: avoids strongly calcareous soil, locally common mainly in mid and high mountains, rare in lowlands; much less frequent in planted larch. Catalogue 600-1600 m consistent but no numbers found.

triggers: No numeric triggers; needs consistently wet, mossy sites (awl.ch). Aug-Nov, late summer and autumn.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Matches catalogue on hosts, wet mossy calcareous sites and season. awl.ch: mountain conifer forests, locally frequent, declining; en.wikipedia pine near seashore. Numeric elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Acid soil and Betula/Picea confirmed. Sources also list pine and beech (oak only in one). Season Jun-Oct (de.wikipedia) vs Jul-Oct (pilzmuseum). Nutrient-poor moist acid soils incl. moorland; elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Sources: Jun-Oct (catalogue Jul-Oct). de.wikipedia: mainly needle litter in old spruce forest, soils basic to neutral; fungiversum also light broadleaf woods and parks. Scattered in uplands, frequent in S. Germany, rare in N.

triggers: No triggers stated. Warmth-loving submediterranean species on south-exposed calcareous beech and oak forests.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Hosts match. Sources stress calcareous soil and very rare status (RL2 Germany; D in later list); catalogue gives no soil. Season not documented (one find 31 Jul-13 Aug), so months left null. Elevation not found.

triggers: No triggers stated. Avoids waterlogged, nitrogen-rich and heavily shaded sites; likes open pine edges.
conflicts_with_catalogue: Pinus-only host confirmed. Sources: Aug-Oct, mainly Sep-Oct (catalogue Jul-Nov is wider). de.wikipedia: soils acid to alkaline, often shallow over limestone. Spruce-bound L. deterrimus is distinct, so beware misidentification in Romania.

triggers: No numeric triggers. Fruits around St George's Day (23 Apr) in UK, March in Italy, May in Germany; later in cooler areas (en.wikipedia). Moderately moist soil with fresh grass.
